name: Composite nationalism
summary: Composite nationalism holds that the Indian nation is made up of many communities, faiths, castes and ethnicities who together form one nation, and that nationality cannot be defined by religion. Each community keeps its own religion and culture while joining the others in a common struggle for independence and a shared state. Its advocates, from Gandhi to the Deobandi scholar Husain Ahmad Madani, rejected the two-nation theory and partition, and held that Hindu-Muslim enmity was fostered by British rule rather than inborn.
scope: The Indian anti-colonial strand from Bipin Chandra Pal's composite patriotism (1906) and Gandhi's Hind Swaraj (1909) to Madani's Muttahida Qaumiyat Aur Islam (1938), the Azad Muslim Conference and the Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind. It excludes Hindu nationalism and Muslim League separatism, and has no economic program, so most non-communal statements are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Husain Ahmad Madani

universal-healthcare.rationale: Composite nationalism is about communal unity, not economics; an inclusive, all-sections nation-building outlook mildly favours services reaching every community, but the sources are silent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No economic program is documented; Gandhian and Congress-era adherents favoured the poor and labourers, so mild support is inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The sources never address market economics, and adherents ranged from Gandhian village economics to Nehruvian planning to Deobandi traders.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents span Nehruvian state-led industry and Gandhian decentralism; the nationalism itself takes no side.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the inclusive nation-building ethos and Congress-era egalitarianism; sources do not discuss taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Saifuddin Kitchlew and other adherents worked with labour and anti-colonial mass movements, and Madani saw trade-union membership as compatible with his identity; weak inference.

property-fundamental.rationale: No documented stance; Gandhian trusteeship and constitutional property rights pull in different directions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: British commercial exploitation was a grievance of the movement, so mild support for regulation is inferred, not stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: An inclusive nation-building view and Gandhi's concern for the poorest make welfare cuts unlikely to appeal, though sources are silent.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by composite nationalism; Gandhian trusteeship is not the same as worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents were themselves surveilled by colonial police and Muslim League rivals; civil-liberty leaning inferred, not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Gandhi opposed intoxicants and Deobandi adherents hold conservative Islamic views, so legalisation is unlikely; inferred only.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Communal harmony was the aim and Gandhi blamed incitement for division, so restricting communal hate speech fits; no source states a law position.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement was a mass, consensus-seeking one built on mutual persuasion; strongman rule is not part of it.

state-harmful.rationale: Composite nationalism presupposes a single shared state and nation for all communities, and its Deobandi wing defended a state in which Muslims and others cooperate.

limit-guns.rationale: Gandhi's nonviolence argues for limiting arms; inferred, with no documented stance on gun law.

empower-police-military.rationale: No documented stance; a nonviolent, anti-militarist Gandhian tendency leans against, while the Deobandi wing is silent.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Gandhian and Deobandi moral conservatism points against legalisation; inferred only.

decide-locally.rationale: Adherents wanted one undivided nation yet cultural autonomy for communities, and the sources do not settle the level of government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence favours reform over retribution; the sources do not discuss prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Deobandi and Gandhian adherents were socially conservative; the nationalism itself takes no stance, so this is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Religious Deobandi and Gandhian adherents would mostly oppose; this is inferred, not documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Religious adherents would mostly lean against; inferred and contested.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents hold that religions are respected and kept in public life as communal identities, yet nationhood is explicitly not defined by religion; they are genuinely split on a bigger public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-caste and anti-colonial inclusion of all segments supports correcting injustices, but race specifically is not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; religious and secular adherents differ.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The idea values a shared composite Indian culture while each community keeps its own; preserving that heritage fits, though no text puts it as such.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents were reformers and mass agitators; the sources give no view on pace of social change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Gandhi held that foreigners who settle merge into the nation and a true nation can assimilate; this speaks against restrictionism, though immigration policy is not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial nationalism cuts against, internationalism and Pan-Islamic scepticism are mixed.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-colonial grievance over British economic extraction and Gandhi's swadeshi suggest scepticism; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism is central but adherents were also internationalist and Gandhian; no clear stance on global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial adherents distrusted foreign military intervention, though the sources do not discuss it.

open-borders.rationale: Not discussed; the idea concerns one territorial nation, so open borders are not part of it.

limit-growth.rationale: Gandhian simplicity points one way, development-minded nationalists another; unaddressed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The idea predates and ignores climate policy; no basis for a stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Gandhi was sceptical of modern civilisation while others were pro-technology; unaddressed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; Gandhians oppose, planners favoured.

revolution-justified.rationale: Gandhi and Madani pursued nonviolent mass struggle and joint anti-British action, not insurrection; Hind Swaraj rejects violence against rivals.

experts-over-public.rationale: A mass-movement, popular unity outlook inclines against technocracy; unaddressed.

central-planning.rationale: Nehruvian planners and Gandhian decentralists both sit within the tradition.

land-value-tax.rationale: No source treats taxation of land.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Swadeshi and the anti-colonial critique of British trade favour protecting domestic industry; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nehruvian adherents yes, Gandhian no; unaddressed by the sources.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Gandhian village economy and trusteeship might favour small holdings, but composite nationalism takes no documented stance on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not part of the ideology; its adherents were not communists.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No basis in the sources; an unlikely view for an inclusive nationalism that presupposes an ordinary state.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Joint state-recognised wage bodies are a corporatist device that the communal-unity texts never discuss, so no position can be drawn.

one-party-rule.rationale: Composite nationalism rests on plural communities cooperating as equals; Madani urged Muslims to join the Congress rather than any single ideological party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anti-British adherents backed an independent republic; hereditary rule is not discussed in the sources.

democracy-best.rationale: Equal rights for all communities within a shared state implies democratic citizenship; Madani spoke of equal rights without religious discrimination.

direct-votes.rationale: Composite nationalism concerns communal unity, not referendum politics; none of the sources take a view on direct lawmaking.

workers-councils.rationale: Not part of the tradition; unaddressed.

right-to-secede.rationale: The central claim opposes partition: Madani, the Azad Muslim Conference and Gandhi wanted one undivided India instead of separate states by religion.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal standing of all communities is the premise; no source treats rulers by nature.

political-violence-never.rationale: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj rejects killing over religious disputes and urges persuasion; other adherents did not always take an absolute line.

war-builds-character.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence; the sources do not discuss war and character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents hold nationality cannot be defined by religion and the state treats all faiths alike, but Indian secularism is a model of overlap and Madani wanted communities culturally autonomous.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Madani argued sharia lets Muslims be co-citizens in a secular India, since some punishments apply only in an Islamic state; scripture-based national law is not the program.

military-superiority.rationale: No documented stance; the ideology is about internal unity and Gandhi was nonviolent.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Composite nationalism holds that people of many ethnicities, castes and faiths together make up one nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The tradition emphasises religious and communal unity against a colonial enemy rather than class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The sources demand equal rights across communities but never say whether outcomes should be equalised.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pal's 1906 version included tribal communities as part of the composite nation, but land authority is not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Madani and Gandhi condemned British rule and its harms; reparations as such are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Madani and Afghani-style argument rejected pan-Islamic unity as the Indian strategy; Madani rejected a religion-defined nation, favouring territorial unity of all faiths.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Gandhi stressed duties but the sources do not frame a general priority.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Neither Gandhi's chapter nor Madani's writings discuss the intrinsic value of nature, so the ideology is silent.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is absent from the communal-unity texts, and Hindu and Muslim adherents differ on family size.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj condemned modern civilisation but composite nationalism as a whole did not; split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; religious adherents would be wary.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A twenty-first century issue that the 1906 to 1938 thinkers could not have addressed, so no stance follows.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents appeal to a shared past of coexistence but look to a united independent future, not a restored order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The sources give no view on judging policy by results versus principle; Gandhi's ethical method and Madani's Quranic reasoning might pull both ways.

direct-action.rationale: Gandhi's civil disobedience was direct action, though adherents also used elections and councils.

means-match-ends.rationale: Gandhi held that unity must be built by persuasion and goodwill, and Madani sought cooperation through shared effort, not coercion.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution of goods is not part of the nationality doctrine; Gandhian trusteeship and Nehruvian planning adherents differ.

production-for-use.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhian trusteeship could lean for, others not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim that adherents neither state nor deny; the ideology is not framed around class exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Foreign to the tradition, which stresses communal cooperation among all classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhian village economy is not collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources blame British colonial policy for communal division, not capitalism as a system causing great-power wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-accepting nationalism has no basis for this view.

harm-principle.rationale: Unaddressed; religious adherents would accept moral limits beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Madani and the Azad Muslim Conference sought protection of communal rights and religious communities as culturally autonomous groups.

conscription.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhian nonviolence vs. national defence.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Adherents insisted on staying and fighting jointly rather than leaving; Madani rejected partition as exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: The sources use equal rights and freedom from colonial rule, but never discuss material means as a condition of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Unaddressed; not part of the tradition.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The idea is built on the shared nationhood of many peoples and Gandhi saw communal enmity as a British-fostered myth, not an innate difference.

organic-representation.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents favoured joint participation in the same political bodies.

total-state.rationale: The idea has each community keep its own culture and religion, which a state directing all of life would contradict.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pal and Besant spoke of awakening, but decadence-and-rebirth is not a documented theme.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The ideology is about holding one existing territorial nation together, not expansion.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of power is outside the texts; Gandhi's remark that the English write misleading history is too narrow to settle it.

universal-morality.rationale: Gandhi held religions are different roads to the same truth, which points toward shared moral truth, while Madani's Quranic grounding is not about reason alone; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The texts do not say whether politics should seek one rationally-derived common good or balance communal interests; adherents stress both unity and communal safeguards.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pan-Islamic and anti-colonial adherents (Afghani, Jamiat) oppose; Gandhi doubted a state on religious grounds, but sources do not discuss Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the ideology concerns residents of one territory, not diaspora claims.

revive-national-language.rationale: Unaddressed; Hindustani vs. Urdu debates divided the movement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Management of firms is not a topic in the communal-unity writings, so no position can be inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Unaddressed; Madani wanted Muslims able to run their own schools, which mildly favours choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed by Gandhi, Madani or the encyclopedic accounts of the idea.

economic-freedom.rationale: The linkage of political and economic freedom is not discussed; adherents span Gandhian, Nehruvian and trader-friendly Deobandi circles.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gandhi stressed moral example in leadership, though this is not a doctrine of composite nationalism itself.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial adherents demanded Indian self-rule for the whole nation, though the principle is applied to one composite nation, not each community.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-imperial and nonviolent leaning; the UN postdates the founding thinkers.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Madani argued from the Quran and Gandhi from religion's shared core; faith is respected, not subordinated to reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not discuss welfare eligibility, though Gandhi said settlers merge into the nation.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed anywhere in the sources, so this is a genuine blank.

class-collaboration.rationale: Composite nationalism stresses cooperation across communities; applied to classes this is inferred, not documented.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Respect for shared heritage and each community's culture makes this foreign to adherents.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-colonial solidarity is natural but the sources are silent on a common front; Afghani's pan-Islam was set aside.

workers-nation.rationale: The sources unite communities across a nation, but do not discuss whether workers organise nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Adherents were mixed: religious conservatives and Gandhian reformers.

ban-interest.rationale: Deobandi adherents oppose riba as a matter of religion, but the ideology takes no national-law position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Composite nationalism holds people of all ethnicities and faiths belong in one nation with equal rights and no discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Unaddressed; the state was seen as a shared national vehicle.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is far outside the thinkers' concerns and the sources say nothing about it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The idea has each community keep its own culture and faith within the nation, though Gandhi also said foreigners merge into the nation; assimilation into a single culture is not the aim.

elite-replacement.rationale: Adherents reject the idea of hostile communal conspiracies; Gandhi called inborn enmity a myth.

proportional-representation.rationale: Muslim safeguards were debated, but the sources do not settle electoral systems; Gandhi urged conceding Muslim demands for safeguards.

national-mission.rationale: Unaddressed; inclusive rather than missionary nationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources do not analyse gender hierarchy; reformist and conservative-religious adherents would answer differently.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Unaddressed; Madani blamed the secular elite for partition but did not claim general corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foreign to the tradition and to its religious adherents.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past abuses is not discussed, though the movement itself suffered colonial police repression.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents expected the state to ensure communal equality and welfare.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The nation is a blend of many ethnic groups, and Gandhi said Hindus and Muslims share ancestors and blood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Madani demanded equal rights without religious discrimination for all communities, and the idea holds all peoples are equally part of the nation.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate that composite nationalism never joined.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The texts discuss British colonial rule but not settler states in general, so no position follows.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Madani envisaged culturally autonomous religious communities, and Muslim bodies in India have seen a uniform code as a threat to religious freedom; Gandhi's position was less clear.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Gandhi's chapter asks why change of religion should make people enemies, and Madani spoke of Muslims explaining their faith to others; restricting it by law is not the line.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj rejects killing or fighting a Muslim to protect a cow, and holds persuasion is the only means; a legal ban contradicts it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Indian secularism bars instruction in wholly state schools, but Madani wanted communities to run their own schools; adherents split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The tradition is anti-colonial and views Indian self-rule by all communities as legitimate, so consent underlies authority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance is not part of the sources; swadeshi concerned domestic production, not export surpluses.

population-transfer.rationale: The core of the ideology is that minorities belong in the nation; Madani argued Muslims should stay in a united India.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence supports it, but Madani and others did not take an absolute principle; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The ideology stresses cooperation among communities; unaddressed as a theory of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents opposed the Muslim League's partition goal but sought to defeat it politically.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-colonial arguments against subjection to British rule fit, but the concept is not discussed.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not covered by the sources beyond the demand for equal rights of all communities.

vanguard-party.rationale: The ideology rests on popular, cross-community mass participation; Gandhi drew every section into the movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Gandhi's concern for the poorest is well known; composite nationalism proper does not address it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that has no bearing on the Indian communal-unity doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law questions are not discussed, and adherents including trade-union supporters might differ.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources blame colonial rule, not population growth, for hardship, but do not take up the causal question.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The idea holds the opposite: diversity of ethnicity, caste and faith makes up the nation, and divisions were created by colonial rule.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Adherents wanted representative participation of all communities through elections and councils, so selection by lot is not part of the picture.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Adherents were victims of colonial emergency laws; inferred, not discussed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Food price control is not discussed, though Gandhian concern for the poor might sympathise.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents wanted free joint political participation under equal rights and opposed party monopoly; inferred from the pluralism.

party-commands-army.rationale: Unaddressed; contrary to the pluralist state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Gandhi said settlers merge into the nation; not a restrictive view, but citizenship rules are unaddressed.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representatives' pay is not addressed, though Gandhi's simple living ideal might sympathise; no documented stance.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed; the Congress and Jamiat circles included varied, loosely organised groupings.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources say nothing about whether head of state or legislature should command the armed forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is a Christian-polity question the Indian communal-unity writers never address.

clerical-rule.rationale: Madani argued Muslims could live as co-citizens in a secular India and opposed Maududi's Islamist state; religious scholars as rulers contradicts composite nationalism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhians would not support war but the question is about a Marxist tactic.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Unaddressed; religiously conservative adherents might, Gandhians were divided.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term rules are not discussed; the inclusive democratic ethos leans mildly against entrenched rulers.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials is not discussed, so the texts support neither side.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not in the sources, though anti-colonial adherents distrusted foreign entanglements.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj praised village life, but the broader tradition did not.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Madani and the Azad Muslim Conference opposed partition; the same logic supports unity, though India's division was not 'drawn by an outside power' alone.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The ideology made no claims about the educated; Madani headed a seminary and Gandhi was a lawyer.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Gandhi held that religions are different roads to the same point and each community keeps its own way of life; equal respect fits though civilisational ranking is not discussed.

death-penalty.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhians oppose, Deobandi jurists accept it in some cases.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Religious and Gandhian moral conservatism; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science curricula are not addressed; religious adherents might be sympathetic but the sources are silent.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Religious and Gandhian moral conservatism; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The idea has all residents of the territory forming one nation, favouring territorial rather than blood citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Each community keeps its own culture and Madani wanted Muslims able to run their own schools; language support follows from cultural autonomy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Madani's picture is of culturally autonomous communities, and Muslim personal law in India is retained; exemptions fit that autonomy.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style nonconformity is absent from the sources; religious adherents value custom, reformers might differ.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not discussed in the sources, so there is no basis for a stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Unaddressed; some Congress adherents yes, others focused on political freedom.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Indian nationalists, including Congress and Jamiat circles, supported a constituent assembly of all communities; not specifically documented in these sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not addressed; anti-colonial grievances over British extraction do not translate into a stated aid doctrine.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the founding thinkers, and Gandhian nonviolence conflicts with Nehruvian security views.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing the head of state is not discussed in any of the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not part of the doctrine and the sources do not mention them.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhi urged conceding to rivals to build trust, which leans against inflexibility.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Gandhian trusteeship fits; the other strands do not discuss it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within Marxism that composite nationalism does not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not covered by the communal-unity writings.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not discussed; the anti-colonial tradition had no defence pacts to consider.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources do not discuss annexation, so no position follows.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents value religious communities running their own institutions, so curbing and subordinating clergy is not the line.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Unaddressed; a unifying symbolic head fits the cross-community ethos.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents opposed partition but by persuasion and joint struggle; force is unaddressed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Unaddressed; cultural autonomy within a single nation suggests some sympathy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Both the Deobandi and Gandhian strands reject sacred rulers; Madani saw Muslims' own religion as separate from state authority.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed by the sources; adherents' economic views span left and right.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gandhi blames British rule and circumstance for Hindu-Muslim enmity, not innate hostility.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Unaddressed; equal rights for all under law implies against.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is wholly outside the 1906 to 1938 sources and no position can be inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed in the sources, so there is no stance.

leader-cult.rationale: Unaddressed; Gandhi was widely revered but did not seek a state cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not covered, and religious personal laws that adherents defend differ on custody rules.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not discussed in the sources on composite nationalism, though Congress adherents later supported zamindari abolition.

refugee-return.rationale: The ideology opposed partition and insisted minorities belong in their homeland; right of return is not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The nation is defined by common territory and many peoples, not by one nationality's claim to land abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Madani argued some sharia punishments apply only in an Islamic state and that Muslims can live in a secular India; legal punishment for leaving religion is not part of composite nationalism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Unaddressed; no national law of dress is part of the program.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed, and the sources concern one existing territory with one nation.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The idea denies that kinship or religion defines a political union; Afghani favoured Hindu-Muslim unity over pan-Islamism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Azad Muslim Conference sought protection of Muslim communal rights, and Madani's communities are culturally autonomous with their own schools and organisations.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Composite nationalists opposed partition and urged Muslims to stay and seek equal rights in India rather than found a separate homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents emphasised religion, colonialism and politics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the sources, so there is no ground for a position.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not covered by the communal-unity writings.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Madani and the Azad Muslim Conference wanted minority rights protected rather than left to majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women are not discussed, and conservative-religious and reformist adherents would differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Swadeshi favours self-reliance, but a shut-off colonial bloc is not what these adherents sought.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not a topic of the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Adherents rejected violent insurrection; Gandhi and Madani pursued mass cooperation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Pal and Gandhi worked against caste divisions, which supports ending inherited privilege; titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The idea has a composite Indian history, but teaching own-nation-centred history is not stated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement is anti-colonial; Madani called the British the greatest enemy and Gandhi attacked the colonial story that Indians cannot manage their affairs.

patriotic-education.rationale: Shared patriotism across communities is central, though flag-and-anthem instruction is not documented.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Unaddressed; adherents favoured inclusion of all sections.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in any of the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist debate about capitalist crisis that is outside the texts.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Unaddressed; Madani's Muslim-world concern is not imperial.

delink-world-market.rationale: Swadeshi-like self-reliance mildly supports, but not stated.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis that the composite-nationalist writers never address.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Madani and the idea demand equal rights with no discrimination on religious grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Protection of communal rights and minority safeguards, as sought by the Azad Muslim Conference and urged by Gandhi, is typically secured by entrenched provisions.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources condemn British rule but do not discuss the legal status of colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Unaddressed; the republican, self-rule ideal of all communities implies election.

minority-veto.rationale: Muslim safeguards were pressed but a single-member veto is unaddressed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Unaddressed in the sources; Gandhi's civil disobedience points toward resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Unaddressed; joint representative politics implies it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Gandhi valued the cow and ahimsa, while Hind Swaraj says life of a human is above it; general animal ethics is inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Gandhi accepted that many Hindus eat meat and rejected conflict over it; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Madani and Gandhi demanded active political participation in the national struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school style claim absent from the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not discussed, although Gandhi argued the British spread a misleading history of India.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-colonial adherents held that British rule drained India; a world-system claim is a stretch, so this is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Gandhi said settlers merge into the nation; office rules are unaddressed.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question; the doctrine concerns Indian communities, not party autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Swadeshi and anti-colonial self-reliance fit; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are not part of the doctrine; the sources discuss holding existing India together, not reclaiming lost land.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The idea is for equal standing of all communities rather than priority for any one.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources predate and do not address constitutional anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources say nothing on comparing fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute that has no connection to the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not discussed in the sources and adherents have no documented stance.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy attention is not discussed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is outside the scope of the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Madani argued Islam allows varied political forms, and anti-colonial adherents rejected imported models; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are not discussed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service selection is not covered by the texts, though colonial-era exam politics were contested.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Swadeshi and anti-colonial economic nationalism; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Religious personal-law adherents would resist; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative-mandate theory is not discussed by the sources, so there is no position.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not covered in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The sources do not address land tenure; Gandhian trusteeship does not equal land held by use alone.

single-official-language.rationale: Cultural autonomy and each community's own culture imply no forced single language; the Hindi-Urdu question divided the movement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership rules are not discussed, though anti-colonial adherents distrusted foreign economic power.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern legal doctrine absent from the sources, so no stance can be drawn.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying is not discussed by the sources and adherents differ on economics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The sources do not discuss foreign funding of NGOs or media.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fertility policy is not addressed in the communal-unity texts.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local purchase limits are not discussed, and cultural-autonomy adherents have no documented view.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is not mentioned by the sources and adherents' economic views vary.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not discuss democracy and war between states.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Gandhi's civil disobedience points one way but the sources give no general view.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial adherents opposed foreign interference; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed by the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Gandhi called the notion of inborn communal enmity a myth, and the idea holds communities are brothers in one joint family.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not discussed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Gandhi's swadeshi favoured locally made goods, so mild agreement is inferred; the Hind Swaraj chapter used here does not itself discuss production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement built mass organisations such as the Congress and Jamiat.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sources do not address the hierarchy of national and international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Composite nationalism's central claim is that nationality cannot be defined by religion; Madani rejected the two-nation theory.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist formula about possessions that the sources do not discuss; adherents accept private belongings in any case.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism is not addressed by the sources; Gandhi and Madani wrote before the Cold War.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Both Gandhi and Madani treat religion as a living value; Gandhi says religions are roads to the same point.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A Marxist-historical judgment about capitalism that adherents never take up.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not link women's equality to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Unaddressed; religious adherents favour the family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The composite Indian culture mixes Persian, Arabic and Sanskrit sources; inferred from the composite outlook.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources do not discuss treaties between states and internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Gandhian village republics fit; other strands do not.

majority-settlement.rationale: Moving majorities into minority areas contradicts the equal coexistence of communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Gandhian third way vs Nehruvian socialism; unaddressed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The idea defines the nation by shared residence of many peoples rather than a prior religious claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No documented stance; an inclusive, anti-persecution ethic.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Religious adherents might, but the ideology is silent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Adherents were an opposition under British rule, and the idea relies on open joint political participation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Madani limited some sharia punishments to an Islamic state; Gandhi urged respect for other faiths; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-colonial at its core; Madani called the British the greatest enemy of Muslims and Gandhi blamed British rule for deepening divisions.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Madani called for Muslims to resist British rule jointly with others, but this religious duty claim is not in the sources.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Madani opposed Maududi's Islamist position and accepted co-citizenship in a secular state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Broad mass participation was a feature of the movement, but the sources do not discuss participatory institutions as such.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a modern framework outside the sources, though Gandhi extended unity to castes.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine is about communal nationality, not a left-right synthesis, and the sources do not discuss it.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxian concept the sources do not take up.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Madani argued Islam does not oppose national unity with non-Muslims and that Muslims can live as co-citizens in a secular India.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Religious adherents might hold this but the national state is built on shared citizenship; split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Cultural autonomy of each faith implies officials and students can keep their dress; secularism in India is an overlap model.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern workplace-law issue outside the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic order is not discussed in the sources, so no position can be drawn.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence, but no explicit stance.

rich-first.rationale: Unaddressed; equal standing of all communities.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is not discussed, but the movement favoured self-rule through public participation, leaning mildly against it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Deobandi interest scruples, but no stance.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lending conditions postdate the sources and are not discussed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim that the sources do not address.

reification.rationale: A Marxist theory of commodity fetishism absent from the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not discuss press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Unaddressed; rule of law is implied by equal rights.

racial-franchise.rationale: The idea holds people of all ethnicities and faiths are equally part of the nation.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is anachronistic for 1906 to 1938 thinkers, so no stance is drawn.

open-government-data.rationale: Open-data policy is not discussed by the sources and postdates the thinkers.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious adherents of each faith might oppose, but the national outlook rejects legal barriers; unaddressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotting a religious minority contradicts the idea; Gandhi urged Hindus and Muslims to live as one nation.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based deliberation is not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Madani argued sharia leaves room for changing rules and that some punishments apply only in an Islamic state, an interpretive approach.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Madani and Gandhi treat religion as valued, and each faith is kept by its communities.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Gandhi urged conceding Muslim demands for safeguards and the Azad Muslim Conference pushed for protected communal rights; power-sharing is the natural form.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Whether charity or the state should help the poor is not discussed; Gandhian trusteeship and Nehruvian state action both sit within the tradition.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern device that the sources never discuss.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is an anachronistic concern that the sources never raise.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The sources do not address marital authority, and conservative-religious and reformist adherents differ.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights for non-citizen residents are not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not covered by the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Gandhian and civilian mass movement; unaddressed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is anachronistic for 1906 to 1938 thinkers, and no position can be inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition politics are not discussed in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Composite nationalism has no economic programme, and Gandhi's critique of modern industrial wealth sits beside Deobandi respect for property, so this is left split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Gandhi's nonviolence points to agree, but Madani and the Jamiat backed the independence struggle without a pacifist doctrine; inferred as split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The nation is described as made up of successive communities and faiths who arrived and settled, not one people continuous from antiquity; inferred from that account.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources never touch sex or gender theory; no position can be inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources are silent on feminist politics; nothing allows a lean either way.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Freedom fighters were honoured, but the sources do not say whether this was sacred veneration; inferred as split between secular and religious idioms.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Gandhi joined politics and religion, but the sources do not frame politics as a cosmic good-versus-evil struggle; inferred as split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The doctrine wants one undivided India holding all its communities and says nothing on diaspora homelands, so it neither supports nor opposes this.

culture-before-state.rationale: Independence and a shared state were the immediate goal, and the sources do not rank culture against the state; inferred as split.

god-not-male.rationale: The sources never discuss how God is described; no position can be inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Madani's Deobandi scholarship treated scripture as authoritative, so a test of scripture by women's humanity is inferred to be disagreed with, though Gandhi reinterpreted traditions freely.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Composite nationalism holds that all communities share one nation on equal terms, so reserving economic life for a majority community is implied to conflict with it.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The doctrine rejects dividing India along religious lines, so reshaping regions to hold one people is inferred to be opposed.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement had no labour programme; independence from the state and parties is inferred from its Gandhian, non-party, anti-colonial stance.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Composite nationalism is silent on economic systems, and its advocates ranged from Gandhian to socialist, so no position is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from Gandhian concern for the common people; the sources do not discuss public services.

second-chamber.rationale: The sources say nothing on legislative design; adherents had no common view.

municipal-property.rationale: Gandhian village-community ownership might fit, but the sources state no ownership model and adherents were split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's preference for decentralised self-governing communities and Madani's cultural autonomy within one state; not stated in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from a general concern for the dignity of working families; no source addresses wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The sources are silent on drug regulation, and Gandhi was sceptical of modern medicine.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: No source addresses ageing research; Gandhian and religious scepticism pulls against it, nationalist modernism for it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; adherents had no position.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; adherents had no position.

person-over-state.rationale: Madani's secular state was to protect each person's and community's religious freedom, which implies the state serves people; the exact principle is inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Gandhi and Madani both argued from religious faith, and the doctrine keeps each community's faith as a living part of public life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Madani and others favoured cultural autonomy and provincial self-rule within India; inferred that they would want such rights secured, not revocable.

gm-crops.rationale: Gandhi's critique of modern industrial civilisation suggests suspicion of engineered crops; inferred, not stated.

dense-cities.rationale: Hind Swaraj, which Gandhi wrote for the movement, idealises village life over cities; inferred from that text.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The doctrine holds that India is one nation of many communities and rejects organising politics by communal interest, as the two-nation theory did.

racial-pride.rationale: The doctrine is about communal harmony, not race; pride in one's heritage is compatible with it but not a theme.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Gandhi's nonviolence implies armed force only for defence; Madani rejected partition on non-violent grounds. Inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Madani argued that a nation rests on a common homeland, not shared language or religion, so people of different languages and faiths form one qaum.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Madani and Gandhi held that all communities form one nation, which favours common electorates, though Jamiat leaders accepted safeguards for minorities.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Gandhi and Madani held that British rule fostered communal enmity and the Muslim League's demand served British interests, so a divide-and-rule plot is part of their case.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the strand has no economic programme and gives no basis for a tuition position.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the strand has no environmental or economic programme, so no position on taxes follows.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's ethic of simple living and trusteeship; the composite-nationalism sources do not address the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: Gandhi spoke of women's capacity for nonviolence and sacrifice, but Madani and the Jamiat were more conservative, so adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's nonviolence and the strand's rejection of military struggle (people in arms is answered no); arms levels are not addressed.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the strand concerned domestic communal unity and did not address diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the strand has no economic programme, so no position on capital flows follows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the demand for a shared state and Madani's secular civic nation; the sources do not discuss arms, but the movement worked within a common national authority and Gandhi's nonviolence.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Gandhi's nonviolence implies personal refusal to kill, but composite nationalists fought for independence and the movement did not call on soldiers to refuse; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: No economic programme is documented, but Gandhian and Congress-era adherents backed workers' organisations such as the Ahmedabad labour association; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No economic programme is documented, so no position on tax credits can be derived.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: No economic programme is documented, so no position on fiscal rules can be derived.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial struggle, which saw British rule as exploiting India, so fairer global rules for poorer countries fit.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The strand sought independence and a shared state through a common struggle and negotiation, not through destroying state institutions; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Gandhi's village swaraj and communal self-rule fit communities choosing their own ways, but no economic blueprint is documented; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: No economic programme is documented, so no position on pricing nature can be derived.

sacred-nation.rationale: The composite nation is a civic union of many faiths, not a sacred community; Madani held that nationality is territorial and religion is separate.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No economic programme is documented, so no position on student debt can be derived.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Madani and Gandhi blamed British rule for division, but the sources do not cast regions of a state as colonies.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi and Madani's common-humanity stance that Hindus and Muslims share one nation and dignity, though the sources do not state a doctrine of human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: No economic or media programme is documented, so no position on public media can be derived.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj chapter on Hindus and Muslims speaks of different religions as paths to one goal, but Deobandi advocates like Madani held Islam exclusive, so this is split and inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the village-centred, inclusive nation-building outlook; the sources are silent.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's nonviolence; the topic is anachronistic and Madani's circle is silent.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement sought one nation across communities and classes, so separate class or communal parties cut against it; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Gandhian reformers and conservative Deobandi scholars would split, and the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Madani followed Islamic law on personal matters and the overlap model keeps personal laws, while Gandhian reformers favoured equality; adherents split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Gandhi promoted Hindustani as a shared language of Hindus and Muslims; inferred from that, not from the cited pages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The ideology has no ecological or liability position and no basis for inferring one.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement was about a united, representative nation; a formal chiefs' role is inferred to be foreign to it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Gandhi's simple living leaned green but the ideology is silent on trading liberty for it; adherents split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Gandhi's reformative view of punishment suggests discretion over fixed sentences; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Cultural autonomy for each community suggests a language requirement would be resisted; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The strand has no labour program; Gandhi favoured voluntary unions but the sources never address compulsory membership.

voter-id.rationale: Voting procedure was not a concern of the strand; adherents' stance is not documented and none is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Composite nationalism holds that nationality is not defined by religion and each community keeps its own faith, which implies no one interpretation gets legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The strand sought a shared state for all communities but did not define democracy; adherents like Gandhi also stressed substantive swaraj, so it is left split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative religious views of Gandhi and the Deobandi ulema who led the strand.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Gandhi's stress on civil liberty and consent against colonial coercion.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Gandhi's village self-reliance and trusteeship ideas, which favour community and moral provision over a state cash-transfer scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the strand's inclusive, all-communities nation-building and Gandhi's call for women's participation in the independence struggle.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: its leading adherents were devout Hindus and Muslim scholars who saw religion as a source of moral life, not a cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its view that Hindu-Muslim enmity was fostered by British rule rather than inborn, a rejection of fixed communal essences.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The strand never addressed gender policy and adherents' views span reformist and conservative; no direction is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Nationality should not be defined by religion; people of different faiths can form one nation.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining claim: believers of many faiths share one nation and religion does not define nationality.

missingStatements.text: A country's religious communities should each keep their own faith and culture while forming a single nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Gandhi and Madani wanted each community to retain its way of life inside a united India.

missingStatements.text: Hostility between religious communities is largely the product of outside rule, not inborn.
missingStatements.rationale: Gandhi called inborn Hindu-Muslim enmity a myth revived under British rule.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow causal claim about colonial history; the position is not about what the state should do and is not contested across ideologies.

notes: Composite nationalism is a nationality doctrine, not an economic program, so most economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences. Critics such as Arshad Alam argue Madani saw it as temporary.
